title: Silimba
summary: The silimba is the xylophone of the Lozi people of western Zambia: wooden keys over large gourd resonators, played with a stick in each hand, often beside drums. Here twelve keys follow a scale of seven nearly equal steps.
howToPlay: Twelve keys lie in order of pitch, shortest and highest on the right.
Strike each key as its note lands on it.
Notes on the half beat make the lilt, so listen for the pairs of strokes.
Start with the two hands woven, then try the slow walking line and the falling stairs.
rules: The scale divides the octave into seven almost equal steps, an approximation of the tuning used on many southern African xylophones; makers' tunings vary.
Twelve keys are shown; real silimbas can have more.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
heritageNote: Silimba players of western Zambia often perform with drums and singers. Each gourd under a key is chosen and tuned to sing with it.
credits: Tradition: Lozi silimba music of western Zambia; figures written for this game
